research_rationale:
EO 13549 (75 FR 51609, signed 2010-08-18, published 2010-08-23) establishes the Classified National Security Information Program for State, Local, Tribal and Private Sector (SLTPS) entities. I read the held Federal Register text in full (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13549.txt, six pages, 21,253 characters). The 62-clause inventory follows the order's own structure: section 1 (sections 1.1-1.3 and paragraphs (a)-(j)), section 2 (the Secretary of Homeland Security as Executive Agent), section 3 (the SLTPS Policy Advisory Committee, paragraphs (a)-(d)), section 4 (Executive Agent duties (1)-(6) and paragraphs (b)-(d)), section 5 (definitions (a)-(m)), section 6 (general provisions (a)-(i)) and section 7 (effective date). The inventory also carries a fragment, 'sec6-b-13526', which is only the closing word of the list of authorities in section 6(b) and is decided with it. Later instruments: none of the held texts that cite the number amends, revokes or supersedes the order. EO 13587 (section 7(b) and (c)), EO 13636, EO 13691 (which amends EO 12829, not this order), EO 13764 (a civil-service rule referring to the order) recite it; EO 13591 and EO 13652 print 'Executive Order 13549, as amended' for the SLTPS Policy Advisory Committee but no held instrument amends the order, and the OFR catalog lists only continuation and cross-reference edges. The eight biennial Federal Advisory Committee Act continuation orders (EO 13591, 13652, 13708, 13811, 13889, 14048, 14109, 14354) continue the Committee created by section 3; EO 14354 (signed 2025-09-29) continues it until September 30, 2027, which covers 2026-10-14. They are listed as later events on section 3 and are not amendments. Section 7 makes the order effective 180 days after August 18, 2010 (2011-02-14) except section 3, which was effective at once; section 7 is therefore recorded as terminated by its own terms on 2011-02-14 while the provisions it dates continue. Current predicate: the order's own held text read with the three bounded searches, whose coverage notes I read (U.S. Code release point 119-121 current through 2026-10-09; eCFR point-in-time 2026-10-14; OFR catalog of 6,941 records and 17,746 saved order texts). The Code extracts (the note under 50 U.S.C. 3161, 6 U.S.C. 662 and 124h-1 and their References in Text notes, which still cite the order) are leads I read; the release-point zip is held only as a custody record, so none is cited as a source. The bounded searches found no revocation. The text relied on is the held official Federal Register text; no transcription is used. The implementing directive that section 1.2 directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to issue within 180 days is not held, and the held evidence does not show whether it was issued; see the independent-command check.

No held instrument revokes, supersedes or amends it: the OFR catalog edges naming EO 13549 as target are the continuation orders EO 13652, 13708 and 13811; EO 13587, 13636, 13691 and 13764 mention the order without a change provision (the dossier's 'cited by number, no change provision located' for EO 12963, 14045 and 14089 is the continuation-order texts); the three bounded searches returned only mentions and continuations. The phrase 'as amended' in EO 13591 and EO 13652 names no amending instrument and none is held.","independent_command_check":"Section 1.2 contains a time-limited command: an implementing directive is to be issued by the Secretary of Homeland Security within 180 days of the date of the order. That is a deadline, not an end, and the held evidence does not show performance; it is an independent command inside the lead clause, and the lead clause is decided on its continuing establishment-and-policy command, which does not depend on that directive. Section 4(d)(2) and section 1.3(i) (reconciliation within a reasonable period) are standing duties without a stated completion date.","savings_check":"The order has not been revoked, so no savings clause is engaged; the held text contains none.","scope_check":"Inventory: 62 clauses matching the held text, with section 1.1-1.3 as one lead clause, paragraphs 1.3(a)-(j), sections 2-4 and their sub-paragraphs, definitions 5(a)-(m) with their sub-items, general provisions 6(a)-(i), and section 7. The fragment sec6-b-13526 is a one-word residue of section 6(b) and is treated as part of that clause. Section 3 and section 7 are handled separately because of the committee continuation and the effective-date mechanics."}
